title: Introduction to Derivatives: Futures, Forwards, and Systemic Risk
prerequisites: Basic understanding of financial markets and currencies
learningOutcomes: Distinguish standardized exchange-traded futures from customized bilateral OTC forward contracts.
Calculate cash flows for hedging foreign currency inflows and outflows using bank bid/offer forward quotes.
Evaluate the terminal payoff profiles for long and short forward positions: S_T - K and K - S_T.
Analyze how extreme leverage (e.g., Lehman's 31:1 ratio) transforms bilateral OTC networks into systemic contagion.
Explain post-2008 regulatory mandates including Central Counterparty (CCP) clearing and trade repository reporting.

sections.title: Contract Architecture: Exchange Futures vs. OTC Forwards
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Contrast standardized exchange-traded instruments against customized over-the-counter agreements.
keyPoints: Futures trade on organized exchanges with standardized contract sizes and delivery dates.
Forwards are private bilateral agreements traded in OTC markets with custom terms.
Futures eliminate credit risk through central clearinghouse novation; forwards carry direct default risk.

sections.title: Corporate Hedging Mechanics & Bank FX Quotes
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Apply bank bid and offer quotes to lock in future domestic currency cash flows.
keyPoints: Corporate hedgers eliminate foreign exchange uncertainty by locking in forward rates.
Importers buying foreign currency pay the bank offer rate.
Exporters selling foreign currency receive the bank bid rate.
sections.numericalApplication: ImportCo locks in £10,000,000 at 1.6005 offer to pay exactly $16,005,000 in 90 days.

sections.title: Payoff Profiles & Terminal Mathematical Symmetry
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Derive and evaluate long and short terminal payoff formulas for forward contracts.
keyPoints: Long forward payoff is linear: Payoff = S_T - K.
Short forward payoff is the exact mirror: Payoff = K - S_T.
Forward contracts have zero initial cost, making payoff identical to profit.
sections.formulaUsed: Payoff_long = S_T - K, Payoff_short = K - S_T

sections.title: Leverage, Capital Fragility, and Systemic Contagion
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Examine how uncollateralized derivative exposures and extreme leverage cause institutional collapse.
keyPoints: Lehman Brothers operated at 31:1 leverage, leaving less than a 3.3% equity cushion.
Lehman held over 900,000 derivative transactions with thousands of counterparties.
Bilateral interconnectedness created ripple effects and gridlock throughout the financial system.

sections.title: Market Scale & Post-2008 Regulatory Architecture
sections.pedagogicalObjective: Synthesize the post-2008 Dodd-Frank and international reforms transforming OTC markets.
keyPoints: The global OTC derivatives market reached $630 trillion in total notional principal.
Standardized OTC trades are now mandated to clear through Central Counterparties (CCPs).
All trades must be reported to central trade repositories for regulatory transparency.

misconceptions.misconception: Believing a forward contract guarantees a profit compared to future spot prices.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: The author demonstrates that hedging provides price certainty, not profit maximization. If spot drops below K, the long hedger still pays K.

misconceptions.misconception: Assuming high leverage multiplies gains without impacting bankruptcy risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: The author shows that 31:1 leverage means a minor 3.3% asset decline completely wipes out equity capital, triggering insolvency.

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: ImportCo has an account payable of £10 million due in 90 days. The bank quotes GBP/USD spot at 1.6200/1.6205 and 90-day forward at 1.6000/1.6005. To lock in dollar cash outflow, ImportCo must enter a forward contract.
activeRecallQuiz.question: Which forward rate does ImportCo lock in, and what is their total USD expenditure?
activeRecallQuiz.correctAnswer: ImportCo buys GBP at the bank offer rate of 1.6005, fixing expenditure at exactly $16,005,000.
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: When purchasing foreign currency from a market-maker bank, the client pays the offer price of 1.6005. Multiplying £10,000,000 by 1.6005 yields exactly $16,005,000 locked in cash flow.

coreTakeaways: Futures contracts are standardized and exchange-cleared with zero credit risk, while forwards are customized bilateral OTC contracts.
Corporate hedgers eliminate currency volatility: buyers pay the bank offer price and sellers receive the bank bid price.
Excessive leverage and uncollateralized OTC bilateral exposures transform individual counterparty failure into global systemic contagion.
